label: MR
reasoning: The row's own acceptance line states 'No command decides this one; his own eye is the check,' which under rule 12/27 (as referenced in the closing-work section) is one of the three cases where the human's own eye is genuinely the gate — a taste call the row itself named at acceptance, not an ordinary buildable result that a command, test, or plain read already confirms. The section 'A shown result closes the work; the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery' explicitly reserves closing without his eye for cases where a row's definition of done does not name his eye as the check; here the definition of done, set weeks ago, does exactly that, so this delivery falls outside the ordinary case even though the test passes and the page was opened and verified to render as described. Because the acceptance criterion itself names his own eye as the check, and he has not looked at the page yet, the Director holds the checkpoint open and shows him the result rather than closing over an unmet condition it cannot substitute its own judgment for.
